The <b>Wormways</b> is an [[Areas (Silksong)|area]] in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i>. Tucked away into the south-west corner of [[Pharloom]], it is a nest of tunnels filled with worms and Plasmium growths.

== Description ==
[[File:Screenshot SS Wormways 11.png|thumb|200px|left|A Grom burrowing]]
The Wormways consists of dark, sandy caverns infested with burrowing [[Groms|worms]], whose ceaseless churning leaves the rock and bone unstable and whose presence renders most of the area dangerous and difficult to navigate.<ref>[[Shakra]]: <i>"Poshanka! It is a difficult task to track anything in these caverns while the worms ceaselessly churn the rock."</i></ref><ref>[[Grom]] [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"They ceaselessly churn through rock and bone without ever seeming to rest. Do they have a destination? Or are they compelled to dig forever deeper?"</i></ref>

The Wormways is primarily populated by burrowing worms known as [[Grom]]s and their young, the [[Gromling]]s. Most of the caverns consist of tight, winding tunnels and spiked pits that make traversal around these enemies difficult. Interspersed throughout the Wormways are [[Plasmium Bud|Plasmium buds]], which are being studied by the [[Alchemist Zylotol]] in his lab at the north of the area. 

There is a utility shaft in the approximate centre of the caverns containing several [[Winged Pilgrim]]s; it divides the entrances to the Wormways from the bulk of the actual area. At the bottom of the utility shaft is a trapdoor that needs to be unlocked from above.

At the lower entrance is a long, horizontal room inhabited by the [[Craggler]], and later, by several [[Cragglite]]s in Act 2.<ref group="Note">More specifically, the Craggler must have been killed, the Citadel's enemies must have been woken, and Hornet must have rested at a bench outside the Wormways, [[Mosslands]], and [[the Marrow]].</ref> West of this room is a door locked with a [[Simple Key (Silksong)|Simple Key]] which leads to a path through the Wormways that can be followed (without having the [[Cling Grip]]). The upwards path leads directly to [[Shellwood]] and is an alternate path to [[Bellhart]].<ref group="Note">This path bypasses the [[Far Fields]] route to Bellhart, and allows Hornet to free Bellhart without entering its Haunted state or go through Haunted Bellhart's west entrance to skip the [[Moorwing]] fight. Skipping Haunted Bellhart unlocks some dialogue with Shakra and the residents of Bellhart after freeing them.</ref> Additionally, the downwards path past the Simple Key door leads to [[Bonegrave]].

== History ==
The Wormways was once travelled by pilgrims long ago in Pharloom's history. However, at some unknown point, it was abandoned and became a nesting ground for the voracious worms.<ref>[[Shakra]]: <i>"There are signs that pilgrims once travelled even these crumbling paths, long ago. Now only the voracious worms nest here."</i></ref> In the past, the [[Weavers]] used the caverns as the location of Weavenest Karn, although at present, Karn is completely abandoned, likely due to the Weavers having long left the kingdom.

Shortly before Hornet's arrival in Pharloom, the [[Alchemist Zylotol]] brought the Plasmium to the Wormways under his master's guidance, intending to study how the substance flourished in a foreign environment.<ref>[[Alchemist Zylotol]]: <i>"Plasmium was discovered by my master at the farthest edge of Pharloom, hidden deep in salt-stricken waters. I brought it to these caves under her direction, to study how it flourishes in a foreign place."</i></ref> His assistant, [[Zango]], was responsible for planting Plasmium seeds around the Wormways.<ref>[[Alchemist Zylotol]]: <i>"Before he went and died, my previous assistant seeded the warrens below with Plasmium buds."</i></ref>

=== Act 3 ===
In Act 3, as a result of the Alchemist Zylotol's experiments with the Plasmium, large chunks of the Wormways become [[Lifeblood#Mutation|plasmified]], with the substance having spread through most of the caverns, deforming the environment and its fauna. Groms and Gromlings have been mutated into [[Plasmidas]]es and [[Plasmid]]s respectively, and [[Plasmium Cocoon]]s have sprouted in a few locations. Most of these changes apply only to the western portion of the Wormways; the eastern portion is mostly unchanged from Act 2. Uniquely, all enemies within the Wormways are immune to [[black-threading]].

Zango's husk has been reanimated and given false life by Plasmium.<ref>[[Plasmified Zango]] [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"Husk of an alchemist's assistant granted false life by Plasmium."</i></ref> While Zylotol is left in an immobile state after also being corrupted by the substance, he still continues his [[Advanced Alchemy|research]].

== How to Access ==
The Wormways is located to the west of [[Bone Bottom]] and has two entrances, both of which branch from the cavern stretching up to the [[Blasted Steps]]. The southern entrance is located in the room directly left of Mosshome and typically requires the Swift Step<ref group="Note">While it is possible to bounce on the enemies using the Needle, it is assumed the Swift Step is used to cross the gap.</ref> to access. The northern entrance requires Hornet to pass through Shellwood.

West of the Craggler room at the southern entrance, there is a door that requires a Simple Key to unlock; it bars entrance to the rest of the Wormways. It cannot be bypassed, as the northern connection must be opened from the western side.

<b>Weavenest Karn</b> is a derelict [[Weavenest]] infested by the worms that persist throughout the Wormways. It can be found at the leftmost point of the Wormways; its entrance is on a high up ledge that requires the [[Clawline]] to reach. It consists of a platforming challenge that ends with a [[Weaver Burial Spire]], where Hornet can bind the [[Sharpdart]] [[Silk Skill]].

== Creation and Development ==
[[File:2021 Aspid Map.png|thumb|"Aspid" in April 2021]]
The Wormways in its current form was not initially planned for <i>Silksong</i>; originally, in its current location, was the "[[Cut Content (Silksong)/Areas#Aspid (Cloverland)|Aspid]]" area, a lush clover-filled area that featured [[Cut Content (Silksong)/Enemies#Aspid (Cloverland)|unique enemies]], some of which being the [[Aknid]] and [[Craggler]], both of which being repurposed and not cut. The "Aspid" area had its first rooms created around early 2019, and is seen in the February 2019 <i>Silksong</i> reveal trailer and in a screenshot released in February 2021's <i>EDGE Magazine</i> issue.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pFAknD_9U7c Hollow Knight: Silksong Reveal Trailer]</ref><ref>[https://pocketmags.com/edge-magazine/february-2021 Edge Magazine February 2021 edition], p. 54.</ref> 

Within the Aspid area was what appears to be a [[Bellway]], in addition to a Sub-Area dungeon known as "Greenhaven" or "Grovehome", where [[Green Prince]]'s boss fight is currently located; it appears to have contained a [[Weaver Burial Spire]]. Also located in this area was seemingly a [[Bellshrine]].

Around early 2022, the "Aspid" area was removed, with the Wormways also being added, appearing in its former location. While [[Lost Verdania]] was also added that year and contained reworked and reused "Aspid" rooms, the beginning of Wormways uses reworked versions of the first "Aspid" rooms.

== Trivia ==
* The changes made to the Wormways in Act 3 are reminiscent of the [[Infected Crossroads]] from <i>[[Hollow Knight]]</i>; both replace several enemies with stronger, massively altered counterparts, and involve a normally dull-coloured area undergoing a sudden, vibrant change in colour. This connection is alluded to by Hornet while talking to the Alchemist Zylotol.<ref name=":0">Hornet and the Alchemist Zylotol dialogue: <br><i>Alchemist Zylotol: "These lands have taken the Plasmium well... the soil has drunk it deep, and the creatures bloom so beautifully... have you seen them?" <br>Hornet: "The effect of your Plasmium on the beasts here is all too evident. Great change has been inflicted upon them. There is an echo also of other infections I have witnessed. I wonder at the meaning of it all... or if I am perhaps imagining similarities where there are none."</i></ref>
